Traits define shared behaviour in Rust, similar to interfaces. A generic function can require a trait bound so it accepts any type that implements the trait, and the compiler generates specialised code for each type, which is static dispatch. A trait object behind a pointer, such as a boxed dyn Trait, uses dynamic dispatch through a vtable instead. Default methods, associated types and blanket implementations make traits flexible. Standard traits like Clone, Debug and From show up everywhere, including in [[Rust error handling]].
